Set up Chrome for static image export

Source: R/chrome_check.R
install_chrome.Rd

Makes sure save_image() can start Chrome, without asking: finds a Chrome or Chromium (see save_image()) or else downloads Chrome Headless Shell with chromote, and on Linux downloads the shared libraries it needs that are missing. The libraries come from the system's own package repositories (with apt-get download or dnf download, which need no administrator rights) and are unpacked into plotly.core's user cache (tools::R_user_dir("plotly.core", "cache")), where save_image() finds them. Run it once on a new machine, e.g. before scripts that export images; interactive sessions are offered the same downloads when needed.

Usage

install_chrome()

remove_chrome(browser = FALSE)

Arguments

browser

For remove_chrome(), also remove the Chrome Headless Shell builds downloaded with chromote.

Value

install_chrome(): the path to Chrome, invisibly. remove_chrome(): NULL, invisibly.

Details

Downloaded libraries are kept in a folder for the OS release, and those for other releases (e.g. after an upgrade) are removed when libraries are next downloaded. remove_chrome() removes everything plotly.core has downloaded and, with browser = TRUE, the Chrome Headless Shell builds chromote downloaded.

The downloaded software is not part of plotly.core and keeps its own licence: Chrome Headless Shell is built from Chromium by Google (see the licence files in its download), and the libraries are your distribution's packages (each package's copyright file is kept with it, under usr/share/doc).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
install_chrome()

# remove the downloaded libraries (and Chrome Headless Shell)
remove_chrome(browser = TRUE)
} # }
